ledger.claim: Trip record, GPS trace and fare ledger all carry trip identifier TRP-03206 and agree on the 19:06:03 start, so the same trip is described throughout the bundle. On the governing measurement — POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not trip_record.actual_distance_km, the field for the threshold test — the vehicle was driven 17.66 km against a booked optimal of 16.2 km, an excess of 1.46 km. That excess clears the absolute limb of POL-RD-01 (greater than 0.8 km), and it is well below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality line, so no MATCHING pattern enquiry under POL-RD-06 arises. The rider's own figure of 17.66 km against 16.2 km in the claim is therefore borne out on the trace.

I do not press that a deviation is established, and the rider should know why. The same derived excess — 1.46 km — is 9.01% of the 16.2 km optimal, and POL-RD-01 requires BOTH limbs of the establishment test: an excess greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km. The percentage limb fails, so no deviation exists on this record and the POL-RD-02 optimal-route recomputation, which by its terms runs only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, does not run — however dissatisfied the rider is with the fare. I have also checked the one route POL-RD-01 expressly leaves open on a failed threshold, a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), and nothing is there: the ledger reconciles (3.80 base fare + 13.28 distance for 17.7 billed km + 6.44 time for 23.0 min + 0.80 platform fee = 24.32 charged), there are no ERP or toll lines, no gantry entries and no airport surcharge, so there is no unmatched charge line to correct.

The driver's only answer is his counterparty statement that he followed the navigation. That is a general assertion: it names no artifact and invokes none of the exculpatory clauses the policy provides (POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11, POL-RD-12), and under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. The trip's chat log gives him nothing either: EV-CHAT-03206 is COMPLETE and contains zero messages, so there is no recorded rider instruction of the kind POL-RD-04 needs to exclude any distance, and no driver admission of the route. On the record as it stands, the driver's account of the route is unsupported by any artifact.

No traffic advisory covers this trip. The bundle's only TRAFFIC_ADVISORY artefact, EV-ADVIS-03206-01, is MISSING: weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING — 'No advisory covers the Blk 55 Lengkok Bahru corridor in this window'). I cite that artefact for the absence itself, which POL-GEN-02(3) makes citable even at weight 0.0. Under POL-RD-13 an external traffic cause — a queue, a closure, an incident — is tested against the advisory for this trip and nothing else; with no advisory on file the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, that clause is unavailable, and no explanation of the kind can reduce or excuse any excess that is measured. Whatever the driver's navigation did, the record contains no advisory that could exonerate the route under POL-RD-03.

POL-RD-01 makes the establishment test conjunctive: a route deviation exists only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and both tests must pass. The derived deviation block measures the excess at 1.46 km on a 16.2 km optimal route — 9.01%, less than half the 20% gate. The percentage limb fails and therefore no deviation is ESTABLISHED, whatever the rider's impression of the road taken. The derived block itself records the status as 'no deviation'.

The governing distance is the trace, not the receipt copy. POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace figure governs and the trip record's rounded copy may NOT be cited for the threshold test. The trace records 17.66 km against a 16.2 km optimal, and the trip record's 17.7 km is the same measurement rounded. The result does not depend on which figure is used: 1.46 km is 9.01% of optimal and even the higher rounded figure gives 1.5 km, or 9.26%. Both sit far below the 20% gate, so the rider cannot rescue the claim by choosing the larger number.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold before the burden shifts to the driver at all. The rider's own claim text supplies the shortfall — 17.66 km against an optimal 16.2 km — and her own figure is a 9% variation. The burden is not discharged, the burden never shifts, and the driver is not required to point to any exculpatory clause.

The trace underlying this measurement is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 139 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, a maximum gap of 0 seconds and no straight-line jump over 500 m. None of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs fires, so the 1.46 km excess is a reliable measurement rather than a data failure, no stretch of excess falls to be remeasured as a straight line most favourable to the driver, and no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names is required. The artifact carries weight 1.0 with no issue codes.

Because no deviation is established, the rider's only remaining route to any money is a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), which is available whether or not a deviation exists. There is none on this ledger: the fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines and a gantry total of 0.00, no airport surcharge, no tolls, and a waiting-time fee of 0.00, and every charged line reconciles to the metered distance and time of the trip actually driven. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11's upfront-quote remedy does not arise either. Nothing on the receipt was charged for a crossing or a service the trip did not incur.

A MATERIAL deviation — the only kind that requires the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check — needs an excess above 50% of optimal or above 8.0 km. Neither is remotely approached at 9.01% and 1.46 km, so the profile check is not triggered at all. Were it consulted, the only fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit for that test are driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d, which is 0, against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 264: no pattern could be established, and no upward pressure on the remedy follows. The driver's lifetime counters on that artifact are context only and are not put to this test.

Disclosure of an impaired artifact I rely on: EV-ADVIS-03206-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, and has weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — no advisory covers this corridor in this window. Its absence is citable but it can carry no fact, so POL-RD-03 exoneration is unavailable on the record and the driver does not invoke it. That does not help the rider: POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 are all adjustments that only bite once a deviation is first established under POL-RD-01, and none is established here. A gap in the advisory bundle is a gap in the bundle, not a finding of deviation, and it supplies no amended optimal route against the driver.

The chat log for this trip is empty — 0 messages, truncated false, weight 1.0 — so two things are established on the record and nothing more. First, the driver's side does not invoke POL-RD-04: with no rider message there is no waypoint_hint and the corroboration test cannot be run, so the clause is simply unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses. Second, and used here only to close the rider's corroboration list, the empty log contains no driver admission of a route change — the one item on POL-RD-07(ii)'s list that could have told against the driver. The record is silent on the route, and silence on this record is not evidence of deviation.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. The trip identifiers on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown all read TRP-03206; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); no timestamp on any admitted artifact runs backwards or disagrees by more than 10 minutes; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact; no charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record; and both sides are not supported by comparable contradictory evidence, because the rider's side rests on her own framing and the driver's statement is unrebutted. The case is therefore to be decided on the money, not sent to a reviewer.

The outcome that follows is NO_ACTION, and under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative: it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are and never restores a charge. Here the rider filed, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so preserving the present state preserves the fare the driver earned on a trip the evidence shows was not a deviation. The driver's statement that he followed the navigation is consistent with a 9% variation below every threshold in POL-RD-01, and nothing in the bundle contradicts it.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the decisive measurement and I accept their claims on it; the disagreement the rider filed is a disagreement with the policy gate, not with the facts.

What the record shows. Trip TRP-03206; the rider filed on 25 Aug 2026. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-03206 — 139 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, weight 1.0, no issue codes) records 17.66 km driven. The booked optimal route on the trip record (EV-TRIP-03206) is 16.2 km. The excess is 1.46 km, which is 9.01% of the optimal route.

Why there is no refund. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH limbs of its establishment test: the excess must be greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km. The absolute limb passes (1.46 km > 0.8 km). The percentage limb fails, and fails widely: 9.01% against a 20% gate. One failed limb means no deviation is established — the derived block itself records the status as 'no deviation' — and so POL-RD-02, which by its terms runs only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, does not run. There is no optimal-route fare recomputation and no refund. The trace governs over the trip record's rounded 17.7 km copy under POL-RD-01, but that makes no difference: even the rounded figure is only about 9.26%. The far higher materiality line (50% or 8.0 km) is not approached, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered at all; were it consulted, the only fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 allow are deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 264, which establish no pattern, so no driver-conduct referral arises.

To the rider, on the fare. The ledger reconciles line by line: base fare 3.80 + distance 13.28 (17.7 billed km at 0.75/km) + time 6.44 (23.0 min at 0.28/min) + platform fee 0.80 = 24.32 charged. There is no ERP line, no toll, no gantry entry, no airport surcharge and a waiting-time fee of 0.00, so there is no unmatched or phantom charge line to correct under POL-RD-09(4) — the one route POL-RD-01 leaves open whether or not a deviation exists. The fare model is METERED, so the upfront-quote remedy in POL-RD-11 does not arise. The 17.66 km figure in your claim is the trace figure and I have used it; it simply falls below the policy's percentage gate, and a 1.46 km difference on a 16.2 km route is the kind of ordinary variation POL-RD-01 exists to keep out of refunds.

To the driver. Your statement that you followed the navigation cites no artifact and invokes none of the exculpatory clauses the policy provides (POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11, POL-RD-12), so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight to excuse any excess. That makes no difference here, because nothing needed excusing. The chat log (EV-CHAT-03206) is empty, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and no rider instruction was recorded. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-03206-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (no advisory covers the Blk 55 Lengkok Bahru corridor in this window); it can carry no fact, its absence is citable, and because you advanced no traffic excuse citing it, POL-RD-13 leaves it a gap in the bundle rather than an escalation under POL-RD-10(5).

Escalation checks. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: confidence is above the 0.70 floor; the identifiers on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown all read TRP-03206; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) (no gap, no jump over 500 m, sampling interval 10 s); timestamps agree; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing cited artifact; no computed refund exceeds any cap; the two sides' evidence is not mutually contradictory; and every charge line has a counterpart in the trace and trip record. Nothing is referred, because POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review and POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity each require a finding this case does not produce.

Confidence. The deciding facts — the 17.66 km trace distance, the 16.2 km optimal and the 9.01% excess — are carried by EV-GPS-03206 and EV-TRIP-03206, each at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and 0.95 is set within it. The counterparty statement carries no weight multiplier and does not enter the cap.

Outcome. NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03: the filing party's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands. fare_breakdown.payment_status remains CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00; the SGD 2.50 contested is neither refunded nor further charged. This ruling was made without human review; either party may appeal it once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
